# Runtime Pilot Results

**Release evidence, 19 October 2026 (America/Toronto).**
These are bounded, same-project development results, not an adopted standard,
external certification, general agent-safety accuracy or a production SLA.

## What Actually Ran

Two paths processed the same supported inputs and used the same current OPA
policy, local occurrence ledger and GitHub dispatcher:

1. Protocol: JavaScript effect description, separately written Python binding
   and tuple checker, then OPA.
2. Structured baseline: direct Python native-to-structured projection, then OPA,
   without transferring the effect-description envelope.

The live MCP lane used the official SDK's real stdio initialize/list/call flow;
both lanes used Octokit against GitHub, not a mock receiver. The tested profile
only describes the direct issue comment. Notification delivery, recipients,
webhooks and other provider descendants remain unknown.

| Measurement | Protocol | Structured baseline |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Exact mapping/status/reason checks | 108/108 | 108/108 |
| Authorization on accepted mapped inputs | 52/52 | 52/52 |
| Expected allow / deny / review instances | 22 / 28 / 2 | 22 / 28 / 2 |
| False allow on deny or review | 0/30 | 0/30 |
| Expected allows not allowed | 0/22 | 0/22 |
| Masked mapping errors / operational faults, offline | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Accepted-input cold total median, n=52 | 50.391 ms | 48.468 ms |
| Live planned checks | 16/16 | 16/16 |

The offline corpus contains **55 authored cases, 22 base intents and 108 lane
instances (53 SDK, 55 MCP)**, not 108 independent tasks. Accepted mappings
account for 52 instances; the other 56 check explicit nonacceptance. Repeated
variants, shared implementations and repeated policy contexts limit statistical
independence. No population confidence claim is inferred from perfect agreement.

Separately, OPA matched all **26/26 independently specified reference-projection
labels** without using the candidate mapper. "Independently specified" here
means a separate authoring path within this project, not an external evaluator.
The deliberately lossy diagnostic altered 26 body digests: mapping matched
0/26 while decisions still matched 26/26. This demonstrates why decision
accuracy alone can conceal mapping errors. It is an ablation, not a competitor.

## Real Provider Outcomes

The single controlled run used
[this dedicated public GitHub issue](https://github.com/OndCo/Action-Effect-Bench/issues/1).
It started with zero comments and produced exactly **12 new comments**.

| Scenario | Checks across both paths/lanes | Observed result |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Ordinary ASCII and Unicode content | 8 | Authorized; 8 comments created and read back. |
| Current revocation and narrower byte limit | 8 | Denied; no comment created. |
| Partial scope requiring review | 4 | Review; no comment created. |
| Invalid policy configuration | 4 | Evaluation failure; no comment created; not credited as semantic denial. |
| Controlled lost acknowledgment after successful POST | 4 | Initially unknown; 4 new comments recovered by read-only lookup, no resend. |
| Duplicate occurrence | 4 | Suppressed; no second POST or new comment. |

Thus **32/32 planned checks** passed. They are eight scripted scenarios crossed
with two paths and two lanes, not 32 independent incidents. The acknowledgment
loss was deliberately injected after a successful real provider response; it
was not a naturally occurring network outage or an autonomous model attack.

Examples of public observations:

- [Protocol SDK normal comment](https://github.com/OndCo/Action-Effect-Bench/issues/1#issuecomment-6259619239).
- [Protocol MCP normal comment](https://github.com/OndCo/Action-Effect-Bench/issues/1#issuecomment-6259620019).
- [Protocol lost-ack readback](https://github.com/OndCo/Action-Effect-Bench/issues/1#issuecomment-6259633673).
- [Structured MCP lost-ack readback](https://github.com/OndCo/Action-Effect-Bench/issues/1#issuecomment-6259636603).

The known POST response ID must match its GET. With no returned ID, recovery
excludes every pre-dispatch comment ID and requires one new exact body/actor
match. Unique markers and a dedicated single-writer issue bound this experiment.
This establishes new current content after preflight, **not causal proof that
our POST created it**, complete provider provenance or global exactly-once
delivery. A concurrent same-account writer is outside that attribution guarantee.
Local authorization and a remote mutation are not one atomic transaction.

## Cost, Without a Speed Claim

For accepted offline inputs the protocol's median cold cost was **1.923 ms
(about 3.97%) higher** than the structured baseline. These timings include
Python process startup/communication, mapping/checking and a real OPA process.
They are not warm serving throughput or an amortized deployment estimate.

The all-input medians, 0.042 ms versus 44.507 ms, are not useful-task speedup:
more than half the protocol inputs are rejected in JavaScript without starting
Python, whereas the direct adapter processes them in Python. We retain these
values in raw data rather than using them as a marketing headline.

Normal live completion included identity lookup, comment preflight, current
policy evaluation, ledger transitions, POST and fresh GET; MCP additionally
included cold transport/server startup. Its medians were **3,110.848 ms** for
protocol and **3,161.205 ms** for structured, with only **four observations per
path**. This is descriptive evidence, not a performance ranking. Initial rows
overlapped a same-host read-only offline replay; the host was not isolated for
a performance experiment. One-second inter-row pacing is excluded from row
costs and included in the approximately 99.049-second complete live run.

Local runtime: Apple M4 Pro, 14 logical CPUs, 24 GiB memory, Darwin arm64,
Node 22.18.0, Python 3.9.6 and pinned OPA 1.21.2. Exact installed dependency
versions, executable hashes and source inventories are inside the reports.
America/Toronto is the editorial timezone, not a location attestation.

## Evidence and Replay

| Artifact | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [Offline raw report](runtime-pilot-offline-2026-10-19T04-23-54.715Z-6bb423.json) and [.sha256](runtime-pilot-offline-2026-10-19T04-23-54.715Z-6bb423.json.sha256) | All 216 candidate rows, 26 reference-authority checks, 26 diagnostic rows and exact sources. |
| [Offline replay](runtime-pilot-replay-2026-10-19T04-24-39.129Z-61da80.json) | Recomputed 216 rows plus 52 reference/diagnostic records; valid and benchmark passed. |
| [Live raw report](runtime-pilot-live-2026-10-19T04-26-11.245Z-731e54.json) and [.sha256](runtime-pilot-live-2026-10-19T04-26-11.245Z-731e54.json.sha256) | All 32 slots, decisions, fault witnesses, timings and exact provider receipts. |

| [Live public replay](runtime-pilot-replay-2026-10-19T04-26-57.109Z-690395.json) | 32 rows recomputed; all 12 unique comments fetched anonymously and matched. |
| [Pinned GitHub OpenAPI excerpt](../runtime-pilot/upstream/github-comment-openapi.json) | Genuine upstream request/response examples and notification wording, not external governance ground truth. |

[`9f638df994504ba6f5d82c0b5409922a0be7a72e`](https://github.com/OndCo/Action-Effect-Bench/commit/9f638df994504ba6f5d82c0b5409922a0be7a72e).

then run these **read-only** checks from the Bench root:

```sh
node runtime-pilot/replay.mjs reports/runtime-pilot-offline-2026-10-19T04-23-54.715Z-6bb423.json
node runtime-pilot/replay.mjs reports/runtime-pilot-live-2026-10-19T04-26-11.245Z-731e54.json --github
```

Public GitHub may later change, delete content or rate-limit anonymous requests;
the reader must retain an unavailable/changed outcome rather than assuming a
match. These commands never repost. A replay verifies bytes, calculations and
current content, not historical latency, complete execution causality or the
honesty of an operator who could forge both a report and its checksum.

## Verification and Retained Failures

[Linux/macOS CI for the measured implementation](https://github.com/OndCo/Action-Effect-Bench/actions/runs/39199258635)
passed the pinned setup, original corpus, new offline evaluation and tests.
The suite comprises 64 Spec JavaScript, 115 Spec Python, 11 legacy harness,
333 runtime JavaScript and 50 runtime Python methods: **573 methods**, not 573
additional benchmark workloads. Runtime unit fixtures do not create SaaS effects.
The [fresh public-clone verification](release-verification.md) also passed
after a dependency-download/setup failure was resolved with the exact
hash-verified binary cache; both the failed and successful replays are retained.

The [first offline attempt](runtime-pilot-offline-2026-10-19T03-40-48.927Z-769420.json)
is retained as **failed**. A scorer incorrectly distinguished null-prototype and
ordinary JSON objects; the direct adapter also disagreed on some invalid numeric
and Unicode error semantics. Fixes changed the scorer/implementation, not frozen
case inputs or labels. That attempt predates the final source commit; its raw
data and hashes survive, but a complete exact old source tree was not archived.
It must not be presented as replayable with the current implementation.

Before the live run, internal review also reproduced eight gate regressions
covering stale identical content, edited old comments, mismatched response IDs,
configuration changes during awaits and current-policy reload. Each failed
against the preceding implementation and passed after correction. The live
experiment only used the corrected source.

The original offline profile still matched 102/102 expected outputs in each
consumer with 102/102 agreement and zero adapter faults;
[that separate report](offline-consumers-2026-10-19T03-59-16-707Z.md) preserves
its own scope and source identities.

## What Is Ready and What Is Not

The versioned draft, separately written implementations, bounded runtime example,
competent baseline, raw evidence, read-only replay, working paper and
[external seal/run/score tooling](../docs/adoption/external-evaluation-cli.md)
are available for inspection and contribution without an OSuite service.

**External independently authored evaluations: zero.** Actual custody requires
other participants and access controls; a hash or a subprocess cannot establish
independent authorship. No Shuwen protected cases, production tenants, Studio
code or Hook configuration were used. Broader domains, adversarial provider
behavior, full descendants, independently maintained implementations and
production operations are not qualified by this pilot. Those limits do not
prevent public review of the completed bounded artifact.

# Action-Effect Runtime Pilot Quickstart

Editorial revision: 19 October 2026, America/Toronto (EDT, UTC-04:00);
first drafted 18 October. The bounded offline and live runs and both replays
are complete. See the [measured results](../../reports/runtime-pilot-summary.md)
and [working paper](../../paper/manuscript.md). No external evaluation occurred.

This bounded, interface-only pilot compares SDK and MCP issue-comment inputs
through effect-wire and complete structured OPA adapters. No OSuite account,
code, or purchase is required. Start offline; live execution is a separate
authorization, not the default installation check.

## 1. Install Without Provider Writes

Use Git, Node.js >=22 with npm, and Python >=3.9. The OPA installer supports
macOS and Linux on arm64/x64. Setup downloads source, packages, and an OPA
binary; it does not post GitHub comments.

The published Spec prerelease [v0.2.0-draft.1](https://github.com/OndCo/Action-Effect-Spec/releases/tag/v0.2.0-draft.1)
is at `a9b86f4b529a5e330c2a9bf1b8c4c259a7b36e40`, the current Bench
[spec-lock.json](../../spec-lock.json) pin. For a fresh checkout, create two
lowercase sibling clones and use that lock:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/OndCo/Action-Effect-Spec.git action-effect-spec
git clone https://github.com/OndCo/Action-Effect-Bench.git action-effect-bench
cd action-effect-bench
git -C ../action-effect-spec checkout --detach "$(node -p "require('./spec-lock.json').commit")"
```

Run every remaining command from the Bench root:

```sh
npm ci --prefix runtime-pilot --ignore-scripts --no-fund --no-audit
node runtime-pilot/install-tools.mjs
```

The dependency lock pins `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.32.1 and `@octokit/rest`
22.0.1. The installer verifies OPA 1.21.2 against the platform-specific SHA-256
in `runtime-pilot/tools.json`. Do not substitute a policy-engine stub.
If downloading fails, do not bypass verification; an existing binary is usable
only when its hash matches that manifest.

## 2. Test Offline and Replay

These tests and the offline evaluation need no GitHub credential and perform
no provider writes:

```sh
node --test runtime-pilot/tests/*.test.mjs
python3 -B -W error -m unittest discover -s runtime-pilot/tests -p 'test_*.py'
node runtime-pilot/offline-run.mjs
```

The runner prints a new report path under `reports/`. Keep its JSON and adjacent
`.sha256`, including failures. To check the published measured offline report:

```sh
node runtime-pilot/replay.mjs reports/runtime-pilot-offline-2026-10-19T04-23-54.715Z-6bb423.json
```

Replay checks report integrity, recorded inputs, source identity, mapping, and
OPA decisions; it does not repeat provider writes or reproduce original timing.
It refuses source or checksum mismatches. Use the recorded source revision,
retain nonzero exits, and never replace a failed report with a successful rerun.

## 3. Explicitly Authorized Live Run

**This command posts public comments. Do not run it without repository-owner
authorization.** It is fixed to `OndCo/Action-Effect-Bench`, not arbitrary
customer repositories.

The completed study used [issue #1](https://github.com/OndCo/Action-Effect-Bench/issues/1)
and created 12 comments. **Do not rerun that issue.** It is an evidence resource,
not a reusable public test target or permission for readers to post.

- Use a fresh, open dedicated issue, not a pull request, with the exact title
  `Action-Effect controlled runtime pilot`. Obtain its numeric issue number
  from the authorized owner; do not reuse an ordinary project issue.
- Authenticate GitHub CLI (`gh`) as the authorized account with appropriately
  narrow permissions. The runner obtains its credential from `gh`; never put
  tokens in commands, public bodies, or reports.
- Agree on synthetic public content, notification exposure, rate/cost limits,
  and cleanup. The live plan permits at most **12 new comment posts**. The
  runner refuses an issue containing an `action-effect-run:` marker.

Replace `NUMBER` with that approved issue number:

```sh
node runtime-pilot/live-run.mjs --issue NUMBER --confirm-owned-repo OndCo/Action-Effect-Bench
```

Lost-ACK recovery is automatically **read-only** in the runner. There is no
separate reconciliation CLI; exported `reconcileAction` operates on the original
ledger/occurrence. Preserve `runtime-pilot/.runtime-private/` privately and retain
the attempt journal and reports. Never retry an uncertain POST, delete markers
to bypass the guard, or rerun a used issue for recovery.

For a retained live report, optionally check current public GitHub content:

```sh
node runtime-pilot/replay.mjs reports/runtime-pilot-live-2026-10-19T04-26-11.245Z-731e54.json --github
```

`--github` adds read-only GETs, not new comments. It checks current content, not
historical wall-clock execution or complete provider provenance.

```sh
python3 implementations/python/cli.py --contract offline-consumer-v1.1 --basis PATH
```

Options work in either order. Omitted basis uses bundled `examples/synthetic-basis.json`, loaded once. Only the launching caller selects configuration; requests cannot change fixtures, refresh state, fetch references or grant authority. Extra `contract` in a request or description is invalid.

Only the two contract IDs are supported. Unknown, empty, missing-value or repeated CLI contract options are fatal, not `unsupported_profile` or fallback.

JS: `const options = {contract: 'offline-consumer-v1.1'}; const check = createConsumer(options); capabilities(options); handleFrame(frameBytes, check, options);` Third argument selects hello behavior; optional basis/profile remain available. Python: `consumer = Consumer(load_snapshot(basis_path), contract="offline-consumer-v1.1")`, then `consumer.hello()` / `consumer.check(document_bytes)`.

Rollback: restart with `--contract offline-consumer-v1` or omit it; recreate API consumers with v1/omitted contract and align JS capability/frame options. Omitted API contract (also JS `undefined`) means v1; explicit null/non-string is invalid. Python class-level `Consumer.hello()` still reports v1. # Offline Consumer Implementation Profile v1

Implementation design approved in principle by the user's request to begin
independently written consumers. Client date: 2026-10-19. This narrows an
implementation target; it does not redefine `0.1.0-draft.1` or claim full core
conformance. The previous editorial evidence remains historical.

## Scope and Independent Construction

Write one JavaScript and one Python consumer, sharing only this interface,
SPEC, JSON Schema and public example/profile data. Do not translate, import or
call the other implementation. Do not import OSuite or previous Matoi code.
Separate same-project authors are not independent external institutions.

Implement strict byte parsing, schema-equivalent shape checks, local semantic
reference integrity, explicit support/trust errors, selected-member digests and
one finite synthetic refund projection. No network, signatures, live authority,
provider access, effect-bound analysis, CEL, caching, hidden data or deployment.

## Files and Runtime

JavaScript entry: `implementations/javascript/cli.mjs` (Node >=22).
Python entry: `implementations/python/cli.py` (Python >=3.9, standard library).
Both run from any current directory. Both accept `--basis PATH`; default is the
project's `examples/synthetic-basis.json`, loaded once as a startup snapshot.
The profile manifest is `examples/refund-profile.json`, pinned to SHA-256
`dddac40519b57620ca8b6fec558746ed8fb1f6ddf77263fd93cf5b2b582f2e00`.
An invalid/unreadable startup configuration exits nonzero on stderr. It is not
converted to a semantic review. No installation or paid service is required.

Only the caller launching the process selects configuration; a request cannot
change trusted fixtures, fetch a reference, refresh state or grant authority.
Snapshot comparison is not proof of current external state or truthful evidence.

## Local JSON-Lines Adapter

This is a local test adapter, not a new wire protocol for AuthZEN, MCP or A2A.
One UTF-8 JSON request per line, each an object with exactly these fields:

```json
{"id":"case-1","op":"check","document_b64":"BASE64_OF_RAW_DESCRIPTION_BYTES"}
```

`id` is a string of 1..128 Unicode scalar values. `op` is `check`, `canonicalize`
or `hello`; `hello` has only `id` and `op`, the others also require
`document_b64`. Base64 uses the standard alphabet, canonical padding and no
whitespace. Raw bytes, not already-parsed objects, preserve duplicate-member,
encoding and number tests. Limit a frame to 2 MiB excluding newline; raw document
limit is 1 MiB. Read bounded frames and drain an oversized frame before continuing.
A final nonempty frame without a newline is processed. Blank frames are invalid.

Output exactly one JSON object per frame, stdout free of logs:

```json
{"id":"case-1","result":{"status":"accepted_partial","reason":"declared_partial","authority":"not_evaluated","description_digest":"SHA256_HEX","effect_count":1,"unresolved_count":1}}
```

Failures have only `status`, `reason`, `authority`. Invalid framing uses `id:null`
and `invalid_input/transport`; oversize framing uses `id:null` and
`evaluation_failure/limit_exceeded`. Unexpected code failure uses
`evaluation_failure/internal_error`, no input, stack or secret in output.
An invalid document echoes a valid adapter ID, never the document content.
Continue serving later frames after an individual rejected request.

`hello` returns `status: capabilities`, `reason: offline_snapshot`,
`authority: not_evaluated`, `spec_version: 0.1.0-draft.1`,
`profile: https://example.org/profiles/refund/0.1.0-draft.1`,
`numeric_domain: safe_integer_tokens_only`, `acceptance_cache: false`.

`canonicalize` returns `status: canonicalized`, `reason: supported_subset`,
`authority: not_evaluated`, `canonical_b64` and `sha256`. This diagnostic is not
description acceptance. Supported values are objects/arrays, scalar-valid
strings, null, booleans and integer JSON tokens within +/-9007199254740991.
Numbers with a fraction/exponent or outside that range yield
`unsupported_profile/numeric_domain`, not a claim they are invalid JSON.
`-0` canonicalizes to `0`; quantity string `"-0"` is still schema-invalid.
Sort keys by UTF-16 code units per RFC 8785, preserve arrays and strings, escape
as JSON/ECMAScript requires. No Unicode normalization or full binary64/JCS claim.

## Document Processing Order and Results

For a syntactically valid adapter request, use this precedence:

1. Document bytes >1 MiB or container nesting >64: `evaluation_failure/limit_exceeded`.
   Root container depth is 1. Reject invalid UTF-8, BOM, malformed JSON, duplicate
   decoded member names, lone surrogate strings/keys and non-finite tokens as
   `invalid_input/syntax`. Validate complete syntax before numeric-domain rejection.
2. Syntactically valid but unsupported numeric token: `unsupported_profile/numeric_domain`.
3. For `canonicalize`, return the diagnostic result. For `check`, require a root
   object with string `spec_version`; missing/type error is `invalid_input/structure`.
   A different string version is `unsupported_profile/spec_version`.
4. Enforce all constraints of the published effect-description schema, including
   required/extra members, enum/type/length/array limits and URI fields. Failure
   is `invalid_input/structure`. URI validation requires an absolute scheme,
   nonempty scheme-specific part, ASCII URI characters, valid percent escapes,
   no controls/whitespace/backslash; it performs no network or normalization.
5. Duplicate effect/evidence IDs; dangling relation/evidence targets; duplicate
   quantity names; unknown-quantity target absent/wrong/duplicate, or also known:
   `invalid_input/references`. Compare decoded strings exactly. A quantity target
   must identify an existing effect and the selected profile's amount name.
6. Any critical extension: `unsupported_profile/critical_extension`. This consumer
   implements none; it never strips and retries. Noncritical metadata is retained
   in the full digest, ignored for semantic widening, not executed.
7. Unknown profile URI: `unsupported_profile/profile`. Wrong digest for the pinned
   profile: `untrusted_evidence/profile_binding`. No URL resolution is attempted.
8. Coverage other than direct/partial, observed modality or non-declaration
   evidence: `unsupported_profile/evidence_scope`. This consumer cannot check
   an empty upper bound or provider observation and does not fake doing so.
9. Invocation/implementation/context references and mapping ID/revision must match
   the profile's finite local table. Evidence artifact references must match its
   declaration row. Any mismatch: `untrusted_evidence/artifact_binding`. Recompute
   SHA-256 on the complete selected JSON member, never the enclosing file or URL.
   Any digest mismatch has the same result. Every evidence source must equal
   `basis.declaration.issuer` and be a declaration; scope text is not proof.
10. Enforce the synthetic projection below. Bad fixture applicability:
    `untrusted_evidence/applicability`; description disagrees with supported
    projection: `untrusted_evidence/effect_projection`.
11. Return `accepted_partial/declared_partial`, complete canonical description
    SHA-256, number of effects and number of unknown entries. This accepts an
    internally bound declaration only, not truth, authority, a bound or execution.

Stages 4/5 are schema/semantic-reference validation, not policy decisions.
Resource-limit failures never earn correct block/review credit.

## Finite Synthetic Projection

The fixture must have object members `input`, `implementation`, `context`,
`mapping`, `declaration`. Implementation name/version are exactly the profile's
`synthetic-refund-tool` / `1.0.0`; visibility is `declared`. Input operation is
`refund`; `order` and context `account` are nonempty scalar strings; currency is
`USD`. Context destination is `original-payment`, environment `synthetic`.
Mapping ID/revision match the manifest; declaration issuer is an absolute URI.
Remaining fixture strings are bound, not interpreted as code or trusted facts.

Exactly one effect is described, with any unique local `effect_id`:
category `https://example.org/effects/funds-transfer/1`, operation
`https://example.org/operations/refund/1`; known resource namespace
`https://example.org/resource-types/order` with `input.order`; known destination
namespace `https://example.org/destination-types/payment` with context destination;
known data namespace `https://example.org/classification`, value
`synthetic-transaction`; modality `may`, no `occurrence_ref`.
Relations are empty. Coverage and the effect each reference at least one local
declaration evidence item. At least one `unobserved_descendants` unknown remains.

If `input.amount_minor` is present, it must be a nonnegative exact integer string
in the profile range 0..999999999999. The effect has exactly one matching amount,
unit USD, scale `"2"`, and no unknown quantity. If absent, amounts are empty and
exactly one `unknown_quantity` targets this effect and the profile's amount URI.
Missing explicit amount/unknown representation is `invalid_input/structure` at
this final domain stage; a represented but wrong value/unit/scale is
`untrusted_evidence/effect_projection`. Invalid fixture values are applicability
failures, not invented unknowns. Other unknown kinds remain recorded but do not
erase the known projection. No current authorization is evaluated in either case.

## Test and Claim Boundaries

Freeze public development cases before comparing consumer outputs. A separate
case author derives expected statuses/canonical bytes from this interface and
the spec, not either implementation. These cases are exposed internal tests,
not Shuwen holdouts or an external independent benchmark. Preserve discrepancies,
fix records and all-run outcomes; never count two agreeing bugs as correctness.

Results identify exact source/case hashes and runtimes, separate expected-result
matches from cross-consumer agreement, and report unsupported features. Faulty
adapters must make the harness fail, not appear as successful rejections. No
speed ranking, production readiness or full CORE-001..028 conformance follows.

# Offline Consumer Implementation Profile v1.1

Contract ID: `offline-consumer-v1.1`. Date: 19 October 2026.

This opt-in processing contract clarifies startup configuration and final-stage
error precedence for the finite synthetic refund consumer. It supplements
[v1](consumer-profile-v1.md); all v1 rules apply except where explicitly clarified
below. It is not a new core wire schema or a new refund domain profile.
`spec_version` remains `0.1.0-draft.1`, the profile URI remains
`https://example.org/profiles/refund/0.1.0-draft.1`, and the full canonical
manifest SHA-256 remains
`dddac40519b57620ca8b6fec558746ed8fb1f6ddf77263fd93cf5b2b582f2e00`.
The seven original contract/example files and their bytes are unchanged.

## Selection and Compatibility

Both existing entry points accept `--contract offline-consumer-v1.1`, optionally
with `--basis PATH` in either order. Contract selection is a caller-controlled
startup option, never a request field or a value inferred from a description.
Only `offline-consumer-v1` and `offline-consumer-v1.1` are supported. An unknown,
empty, missing-value or repeated contract option is a fatal startup error, not
an `unsupported_profile` response and not a fallback to v1.

Omitting `--contract`, or selecting `--contract offline-consumer-v1`, retains the
old v1 behavior and output. In particular, default `hello` gains no new field.
In v1.1, `hello` returns exactly:

```json
{"status":"capabilities","reason":"offline_snapshot","authority":"not_evaluated","spec_version":"0.1.0-draft.1","profile":"https://example.org/profiles/refund/0.1.0-draft.1","numeric_domain":"safe_integer_tokens_only","acceptance_cache":false,"contract":"offline-consumer-v1.1"}
```

The adapter wraps this result with the request's `id` as in v1. The extra
`contract` member identifies processing behavior, not a replacement
`spec_version` or profile binding. `check` and `canonicalize` result shapes,
description digests, framing, limits and continuation after rejected frames
are unchanged. A request or description with an extra `contract` field remains
invalid under the unchanged adapter or core structure rules, respectively.

The language-local API options are:

```javascript
const options = { contract: 'offline-consumer-v1.1' };
const check = createConsumer(options); // optional basis and profile as in v1
capabilities(options);
handleFrame(frameBytes, check, options); // optional third argument for hello
```

```python
consumer = Consumer(load_snapshot(basis_path), contract="offline-consumer-v1.1")
consumer.hello()
consumer.check(document_bytes)
```

API callers receive a startup exception for an unsupported contract or unusable
configuration, not a per-document result. Omitted API contract options retain
v1; JavaScript's `undefined` contract option also means omitted. Explicit `null`
or non-string contract values are invalid. The legacy Python `Consumer.hello()`
class-level query continues to report v1 capabilities.

## Startup Configuration Versus Applicability

Before serving any frame, the consumer MUST load and validate its caller-selected
local snapshot. The following are invalid configuration:

- An unreadable selected file, invalid UTF-8/JSON, duplicate decoded keys, invalid
  Unicode scalars, exceeded input/nesting limits, or numbers outside v1's
  safe-integer-token-only startup JSON subset.
- A manifest that does not match the pinned complete canonical content.
- A basis root that is not an object, or a missing/nonobject `input`,
  `implementation`, `context`, `mapping` or `declaration` member. Arrays, null,
  strings, booleans and numbers are not objects for this purpose.

Such configuration MUST terminate the CLI with a nonzero exit, no stdout frames
(including no `hello`), and a fixed diagnostic on stderr. Diagnostics MUST NOT
include fixture/input contents, supplied argument values, paths, secrets or a
stack trace. API exceptions likewise MUST NOT embed supplied configuration
contents. Only an omitted basis selection uses the bundled basis in v1.1;
an explicitly supplied null basis is invalid, not a request for that default.
For the JavaScript API this also applies to explicitly supplied `undefined`
basis/profile values. This opt-in rule does not change JavaScript v1's legacy
nullish configuration fallback.

The five required member objects may be empty at startup. Once their shape and
the startup JSON subset are valid, missing nested scalar fields or unsupported
scalar values are fixture applicability issues, not startup errors. For example,
`input.currency: "EUR"`, `input.order: null`, a wrong implementation version,
or `input.amount_minor: 7300` load successfully but cannot establish applicable
refund semantics. A present amount must be an exact decimal integer string in
0..999999999999; null, booleans, numbers, signs, leading zeros, whitespace and
out-of-range strings do not become unknown amounts. Only an absent
`input.amount_minor` permits the explicit unknown-amount projection from v1.

Applicability is a final-domain check, not a new early rejection stage. Document
syntax, numeric support, schema, local references, critical extensions, profile
binding, evidence scope and selected-member artifact binding still precede it.
For example, a stale invocation digest wins over unsupported fixture currency.
A malformed evidence source fails structure, and a source unequal to the
configured declaration issuer fails artifact binding, even if that issuer is
itself inapplicable. No stage is skipped to manufacture an applicability result.
After earlier stages succeed, unsupported fixture values MUST yield
`untrusted_evidence/applicability`, never an invented unknown or acceptance.

## Final Projection Precedence

Replace the ambiguity within v1 document-processing stage 10 with this ordered
sequence. This does not move any check ahead of stages 1 through 9:

1. **Fixture applicability.** Apply all finite synthetic fixture constraints in
   v1. Any failure yields `untrusted_evidence/applicability`, even if the
   description also has a wrong effect count or projection.
2. **Effect cardinality.** Require exactly one effect. Zero or multiple effects
   yield `untrusted_evidence/effect_projection`. Do not pick a first/last tuple
   or inspect one tuple's missing amount as if cardinality had succeeded.
3. **Missing required amount representation.** In that single effect, require a
   quantity named `https://example.org/quantities/amount` OR an
   `unknown_quantity` targeting that effect and exact name. If neither exists,
   yield `invalid_input/structure`, even with unrelated quantities or other
   projection defects. This is a final-domain structure error, not an earlier
   schema check. Duplicate, dangling, wrong-name and known/unknown-collision
   targets already fail reference validation at stage 5.
4. **Remaining coupled projection.** Apply all remaining v1 projection rules:
   category, operation, exact resource/destination/data-class tuple, no
   occurrence reference, empty relations, nonempty coverage/effect evidence
   references, unobserved descendants, and the exact known/unknown amount rule.
   Any mismatch yields `untrusted_evidence/effect_projection`. A represented
   but wrong amount/value/unit/scale, unknown amount when the fixture supplies
   one, or known amount when the fixture omits it belongs here, not at step 3.

Checks within step 4 have the same public result; their internal order is not
specified. Tuples are never recombined. If all stages succeed, return the v1
`accepted_partial/declared_partial` result. Every result retains
`authority: not_evaluated`; none is permission, observation or a checked bound.

The language-local tests exercise each pair of priority classes and repair the
higher-priority defect to expose the lower one. In particular:

| Simultaneous defects | First result |
| --- | --- |
| Bad applicability + cardinality, missing amount or coupled mismatch | `untrusted_evidence/applicability` |
| Multiple effects + missing required amount | `untrusted_evidence/effect_projection` |
| Multiple effects + coupled mismatch | `untrusted_evidence/effect_projection` |
| Missing amount representation + coupled mismatch | `invalid_input/structure` |
| Represented wrong amount + another coupled mismatch | `untrusted_evidence/effect_projection` |

## Verification and Claim Boundary

Run both suites locally without dependencies or network:

```sh
node --test implementations/javascript/*.test.mjs
python3 -B -W error -m unittest discover -s implementations/python/tests
```

CI runs both the frozen v1 and opt-in v1.1 test files through discovery. The
published v1 corpus continues to select v1 explicitly; its results are not
silently relabeled as v1.1 results.

These are exposed same-project implementation and regression tests, not external
validation, new holdouts, certification or full core conformance. The previously
separate JavaScript and Python implementations remain language-local; neither
imports or invokes the other. This hardening adds no domain, dependency,
network access, authorization, provider effect, cache or production-readiness
claim. Frozen v1 publications and historical results are not relabeled as v1.1.

# Draft Change Record

## 0.2.0-draft.1

Added an opt-in `offline-consumer-v1.1` contract with startup configuration
rejection, explicit contract identity and deterministic final projection error
precedence. Added paired-defect and legacy-compatibility tests in JavaScript and
Python. The seven frozen files, core wire version and default v1 behavior remain
unchanged, including the documented historical JS null-option fallback.

Added the GitHub issue-comment profile: exact native invocation and body binding,
partial direct scope, explicit provider-descendant unknowns, and a distinct
authorization integration in the companion benchmark. This is a narrowly
implemented profile, not a claim that legacy refund consumers understand GitHub.

## Public-Checkout Entry Point Repair

During clean-clone reproduction on 18 October 2026 (America/Toronto), an absolute
path through a filesystem symlink caused the JavaScript CLI to exit zero without
reading a request or producing a response. The entry-point guard compared a
lexical argument path with Node's resolved module path. This also affected the
companion benchmark's two command-line entry points.

The guard now compares resolved filesystem identities. A new regression requires
a symlinked CLI invocation to return an actual capability response; a separate
stdin-import control preserves import-safe behavior. The regression failed on
the previous implementation before the fix. Python and the semantic evaluator
were not changed.

The original seven source-frozen contract/example files remain byte-identical.
No test expectation, effect semantics, numeric domain, authority decision or
signature claim was changed. Benchmark reports before this fix remain historical
reports of their named source snapshot, not evidence that symlinked entry points
were covered. The companion benchmark pins the corrected commit for new runs.

# Bounded Runtime Pilot

This directory implements the GitHub Issue Comment Profile 1 from the pinned
companion Spec. It is an executable research/adoption example, not the OSuite
application, a general sandbox, or an independently certified standard.

## Two Complete Paths

```text
SDK or MCP request + configured context
  protocol:   JS description -> Python binding/tuple check
  structured: Python native-to-structured projection
        -> same current OPA policy -> same occurrence ledger
        -> one GitHub POST -> fresh readback
        -> confirmed, unknown, withheld, or duplicate-suppressed
```

Both paths use the same finite native-input restrictions, policy and controlled
dispatch behavior. The protocol adds a transferable description and a second
implementation's binding checks; it is not assumed faster or more accurate
than a correct direct adapter. SDK/MCP envelopes differ, so compare semantic
projections rather than treating their full wire hashes as identical.

Install and execute using [the quickstart](../docs/adoption/quickstart.md).
Results and exact retained reports are indexed [here](../reports/runtime-pilot-summary.md).

## Inputs and Outcomes

- `mapping.mjs` produces a direct **partial** effect declaration; the Python
  consumer checks it against the actual native capture and configured context.
- `authorization.mjs` invokes the pinned real OPA binary and validates its
  output. An engine/configuration failure is not counted as a policy denial.
- `gate.mjs` snapshots the native input and configured provider methods,
  validates provider identity, and reloads current policy after preparation
  and read-only preflight. Descriptor acceptance alone never permits a write.
- `ledger.mjs` reserves an occurrence with exclusive creation and durable
  state transitions. It is a same-host ledger, not a distributed transaction.
- `provider.mjs` uses Octokit with fixed GitHub API endpoints and no automatic
  POST retry. Credentials remain in memory and outside public evidence.
- `mcp-server.mjs` and `mcp-client.mjs` use the official SDK's real stdio
  initialize/list/call exchange. Unknown keys are rejected, not stripped.
- `replay.mjs` verifies retained byte identities and reruns local mapping/OPA.
  `--github` performs unauthenticated, read-only current-content checks.

The raw processing states (`accepted_partial`, `invalid_input`,
`unsupported_profile`, `untrusted_evidence`, `evaluation_failure`) are separate
from `allow`/`deny`/`review` and separate again from the observed provider result.
The external-evaluation CLI likewise seals inputs and labels separately before
running/scoring; see [its contract](../docs/adoption/external-evaluation-cli.md).

## Trust and Non-Claims

Local code, profile installation, policy files, configured principal/class,
ledger storage and host filesystem are trusted. The implementation identity is
a **declaration**, not an attested binary or proof of GitHub's internal code.
The native capture must come from the path that actually dispatches the request;
a hash cannot make a dishonest capture truthful.

GitHub explicitly documents notification behavior for comment creation. We
represent only the direct comment and retain unknown downstream recipients,
delivery, webhooks and internal descendants. Partial scope is admitted only
with the experiment's explicit policy choice on synthetic public resources.
No notification or transitive-closure completeness is claimed.

Current local authorization and the remote POST are not atomic. A revocation
after the final local check may race with dispatch. A local occurrence ledger
does not provide global exactly-once delivery, automatic crash-lock recovery,
multi-tenant isolation, distributed quota handling, or a provider idempotency key.
If delivery might have occurred, the reservation stays consumed and recovery
only queries. Missing or ambiguous observations remain unknown.

Readback must match the POST response ID when that ID is known. With a lost
acknowledgment, recovery excludes every comment ID recorded before dispatch
and requires one new exact content/actor match. Preexisting matching content
is withheld before dispatch. This test uses a dedicated issue, unique body
markers and one controlled writer. A new matching comment establishes current
content after preflight, not causal proof that this specific POST created it:
a concurrent same-account writer or provider-side mutation is outside that
attribution guarantee. This distinction is recorded in `recovery_evidence`.

The live runner records each scheduled/result step in a fsynced attempt journal,
stops new writes after an unexpected result, and refuses to reuse an issue
already containing a pilot marker. It does not silently create a new occurrence
to retry an uncertain write. Keep partial journals and the private local ledger
if interrupted; use read-only reconciliation instead of rerunning the live CLI.

## Evaluation Boundaries

The 55-case/22-intent development corpus is same-project, AI-assisted and public.
It was hidden from candidate implementers until its pre-result freeze, not
withheld from implementation development forever. The original incorrect freeze
ordering statement and its corrections are retained in the custody history.
The real live subset is eight scripted scenarios across two lanes and two
strategies, not 32 independent incidents or autonomous model decisions.

The upstream GitHub OpenAPI excerpt is genuine third-party interface material
with a pinned commit and retained MIT notice. It is not independently authored
governance labels. No outside team has yet run the external-custody protocol.
Costs include cold subprocesses and communication where measured; there is no
warm-path throughput claim, tail SLA, or broad customer-deployment qualification.
The `America/Toronto` report timezone is an editorial preference, not a
geolocation or Canadian work-location attestation.

# GitHub Issue Comment Profile 1

Prepared 18 October 2026, America/Toronto. Additive experimental domain profile. The
release is `v0.2.0-draft.1`; the unchanged core wire version is
`0.1.0-draft.1`. The legacy refund profile is not rewritten or generalized.

This profile describes one direct API mutation, not arbitrary GitHub tools,
workflow closures, source-code safety, credential authority or provider internals.
It is usable without OSuite. It does not grant GitHub or local-policy permission.

## Native Input and Configuration

SDK input: `{"lane":"sdk","call":{"owner":"OndCo","repo":"Action-Effect-Bench","issue_number":1,"body":"Synthetic test"}}`.
MCP input: `{"lane":"mcp","call":{"name":"add_issue_comment","arguments":{"owner":"OndCo","repo":"Action-Effect-Bench","issue_number":1,"body":"Synthetic test"}}}`.
These are local capture envelopes. The MCP lane uses actual MCP `tools/call`
transport; this envelope is not a replacement protocol.

Only the shown keys are accepted. Names are ASCII and path-safe: owner matches
`[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]{0,38}`; repo matches
`[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,100}` but is neither `.` nor `..`. Issue number is a positive
integer at most 2147483647, excluding booleans. Body is a nonempty Unicode-scalar
string with at most 8192 UTF-8 bytes. No normalization, path unescaping, URL
resolution, template expansion or caller-supplied endpoint is supported.

The caller configures `context` with a nonempty `principal`, nonempty
`data_class`, and `implementation: "github-comment-bridge/1"`. Missing facts
produce `untrusted_evidence/missing_context`; a different implementation produces
`untrusted_evidence/implementation_binding`. This is a declared implementation
identity, not attestation of arbitrary SaaS code. Executable/package source
hashes are recorded separately by the experiment. Classification comes from the
trusted test configuration, not text analysis; no DLP classifier is claimed.

## Deterministic Processing

1. Reject malformed native shape or parameters as `invalid_input/native_input`.
2. An otherwise shaped MCP invocation with another tool name produces
   `unsupported_profile/operation`; no arguments of that tool are executed.
3. Check context presence, then implementation identity.
4. Produce a direct, partial declaration. The downstream unknown is retained.
5. A consumer validates core structure and every binding, then the exact coupled
   tuple and required body-digest extension. Unsupported critical extensions
   cannot be stripped. A failed binding yields
   `untrusted_evidence/description_binding`, never permission.

The complete native envelope, complete context and the profile manifest are
separate JSON digest preimages. The declared implementation preimage is
`{"id":"github-comment-bridge/1","kind":"declaration"}`. The declaration
artifact is `{"native":N,"context":C,"profile_digest":H(P)}`. Canonical JSON
uses the core's safe-integer subset of RFC 8785. No reference is fetched.
Local references are `urn:action-effect:github-comment:invocation`, `:context`,
`:implementation`, and `:declaration` respectively. Mapping id is the manifest
URI with `#mapping`, revision `1`, digest H(P). Evidence source is manifest URI.

Acceptance returns `accepted_partial/declared_partial`,
`authority: not_evaluated`, full description digest, and a checked projection:

```json
{"operation":"create_issue_comment","repository":"OndCo/Action-Effect-Bench","issue_number":1,"endpoint":"https://api.github.com/repos/OndCo/Action-Effect-Bench/issues/1/comments","body_sha256":"hex SHA-256 of exact UTF-8 body","body_bytes":14,"data_class":"synthetic-public"}
```

This illustration's digest label is explanatory, not a valid test vector.
Runtime equivalence compares checked projections. Full description digests
differ when the native lane differs; they are not cross-runtime semantic IDs.

## Remote Mutation

Exactly one effect, id `comment`, modality `may`, describes comment creation.
No observation, zero-effect bound, transitive completeness or causal graph is
inferred. Coverage and effect both refer to declaration evidence `declaration`.
Relations are empty. Exactly one `unobserved_descendants` entry retains the
manifest's unknown scope. Provider readback is a separate observation artifact.
GitHub's API description explicitly declares that creation triggers
notifications. The unknown scope concerns recipients, delivery and downstream
effects; it must not be read as claiming notifications do not happen.

## Create Comment

The operation is creation of one issue comment through GitHub REST. An update,
delete, release, repository creation or arbitrary request is unsupported.

## GitHub Issue

The resource slot is known, namespace from the manifest, and value
`owner/repo#issue_number`. Comparison is exact, conservatively case-sensitive.

## HTTPS Endpoint

The known destination value is
`https://api.github.com/repos/owner/repo/issues/issue_number/comments`.
Only this endpoint is constructed. Authenticated provider identity and actual
dispatch permission still need separate validation.

## Caller Classification

The known data slot retains the caller-configured class. Live demonstrations
accept only `synthetic-public`; text must contain no customer/private data.

**Draft requiring maintainer review, not write/publication authorization.** [1]–[5] refer to `citations` in order. This task read five pinned files via SDK GitHub REST/HTTPS (runner: Octokit 22.0.1; startup not observed). No tests, mutations or fault experiments ran. Historical pilot results are documentation, not new observations. No actual ledger, journal, receipt or policy was supplied.

## Limits before dispatch

| Boundary | Limit and operational consequence | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Native input | Only documented SDK/MCP keys; MCP tool `add_issue_comment`. Malformed/extra keys reject; another shaped tool is unsupported, not executed. | [1] |
| Resource | Owner `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]{0,38}`; repo `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,100}`, excluding `.`/`..`; issue integer 1–2147483647, not boolean. ASCII/path-safe names; exact case-sensitive comparison. Creation only; no caller endpoint, unescaping, normalization, URL resolution or templates. | [1] |
| Body bytes | Nonempty Unicode-scalar string, ≤8192 UTF-8 bytes, not JS UTF-16 units. Preserve exact text/SHA-256. Local policy may impose a lower byte ceiling; actual policy threshold was not inspected. | [1] |
| Context | Nonempty principal/data_class; implementation `github-comment-bridge/1`. Missing/mismatched facts yield untrusted evidence. Live content is synthetic-public, never customer/private data. Identity is declared, not attested. | [1] |
| Provider listing | 100/page, ≤5 pages; returns only after a page with <100 rows. Five full pages throw `readback_pagination_limit`, including exactly 500 comments. Gate independently accepts arrays ≤500 with unique positive safe-integer IDs. Never use truncated preflight. | [2,3] |

Stop new writes after unexpected results. Preserve the original occurrence; never retry a possible POST. [3–5]

| Condition | Action / interpretation |
|---|---|
| Preflight unavailable before POST | Gate withholds `provider_preflight_unavailable` / evaluation failure, not policy denial. Preexisting exact matching content instead withholds `preexisting_matching_content`. Preserve failure; do not bypass guards. [3] |
| Inflight/unknown, known response ID | Exported `reconcileAction` GETs that ID on the original occurrence/binding. Exact ID, API comment URL, issue URL, body and actor must match. One match confirms with `known-response-id-and-current-content`; failure/mismatch stays unknown. [2,3] |
| Missing ID, complete saved preflight | List comments; exclude every pre-dispatch ID; require exactly one new exact body/actor/resource match. | Missing ID and preflight | Remain `unknown/missing_occurrence_preflight`; no safe ID-less inference or resend. Known-ID recovery does not require the baseline. [3] |

# GitHub Issue Comment Profile 1

Prepared 18 October 2026, America/Toronto. Additive experimental domain profile. The
release is `v0.2.0-draft.1`; the unchanged core wire version is
`0.1.0-draft.1`. The legacy refund profile is not rewritten or generalized.

This profile describes one direct API mutation, not arbitrary GitHub tools,
workflow closures, source-code safety, credential authority or provider internals.
It is usable without OSuite. It does not grant GitHub or local-policy permission.

## Native Input and Configuration

SDK input: `{"lane":"sdk","call":{"owner":"OndCo","repo":"Action-Effect-Bench","issue_number":1,"body":"Synthetic test"}}`.
MCP input: `{"lane":"mcp","call":{"name":"add_issue_comment","arguments":{"owner":"OndCo","repo":"Action-Effect-Bench","issue_number":1,"body":"Synthetic test"}}}`.
These are local capture envelopes. The MCP lane uses actual MCP `tools/call`
transport; this envelope is not a replacement protocol.

Only the shown keys are accepted. Names are ASCII and path-safe: owner matches
`[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]{0,38}`; repo matches
`[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,100}` but is neither `.` nor `..`. Issue number is a positive
integer at most 2147483647, excluding booleans. Body is a nonempty Unicode-scalar
string with at most 8192 UTF-8 bytes. No normalization, path unescaping, URL
resolution, template expansion or caller-supplied endpoint is supported.

The caller configures `context` with a nonempty `principal`, nonempty
`data_class`, and `implementation: "github-comment-bridge/1"`. Missing facts
produce `untrusted_evidence/missing_context`; a different implementation produces
`untrusted_evidence/implementation_binding`. This is a declared implementation
identity, not attestation of arbitrary SaaS code. Executable/package source
hashes are recorded separately by the experiment. Classification comes from the
trusted test configuration, not text analysis; no DLP classifier is claimed.

## Deterministic Processing

1. Reject malformed native shape or parameters as `invalid_input/native_input`.
2. An otherwise shaped MCP invocation with another tool name produces
   `unsupported_profile/operation`; no arguments of that tool are executed.
3. Check context presence, then implementation identity.
4. Produce a direct, partial declaration. The downstream unknown is retained.
5. A consumer validates core structure and every binding, then the exact coupled
   tuple and required body-digest extension. Unsupported critical extensions
   cannot be stripped. A failed binding yields
   `untrusted_evidence/description_binding`, never permission.

The complete native envelope, complete context and the profile manifest are
separate JSON digest preimages. The declared implementation preimage is
`{"id":"github-comment-bridge/1","kind":"declaration"}`. The declaration
artifact is `{"native":N,"context":C,"profile_digest":H(P)}`. Canonical JSON
uses the core's safe-integer subset of RFC 8785. No reference is fetched.
Local references are `urn:action-effect:github-comment:invocation`, `:context`,
`:implementation`, and `:declaration` respectively. Mapping id is the manifest
URI with `#mapping`, revision `1`, digest H(P). Evidence source is manifest URI.

Acceptance returns `accepted_partial/declared_partial`,
`authority: not_evaluated`, full description digest, and a checked projection:

```json
{"operation":"create_issue_comment","repository":"OndCo/Action-Effect-Bench","issue_number":1,"endpoint":"https://api.github.com/repos/OndCo/Action-Effect-Bench/issues/1/comments","body_sha256":"hex SHA-256 of exact UTF-8 body","body_bytes":14,"data_class":"synthetic-public"}
```

This illustration's digest label is explanatory, not a valid test vector.
Runtime equivalence compares checked projections. Full description digests
differ when the native lane differs; they are not cross-runtime semantic IDs.

## Remote Mutation

Exactly one effect, id `comment`, modality `may`, describes comment creation.
No observation, zero-effect bound, transitive completeness or causal graph is
inferred. Coverage and effect both refer to declaration evidence `declaration`.
Relations are empty. Exactly one `unobserved_descendants` entry retains the
manifest's unknown scope. Provider readback is a separate observation artifact.
GitHub's API description explicitly declares that creation triggers
notifications. The unknown scope concerns recipients, delivery and downstream
effects; it must not be read as claiming notifications do not happen.

## Create Comment

The operation is creation of one issue comment through GitHub REST. An update,
delete, release, repository creation or arbitrary request is unsupported.

## GitHub Issue

The resource slot is known, namespace from the manifest, and value
`owner/repo#issue_number`. Comparison is exact, conservatively case-sensitive.

## HTTPS Endpoint

The known destination value is
`https://api.github.com/repos/owner/repo/issues/issue_number/comments`.
Only this endpoint is constructed. Authenticated provider identity and actual
dispatch permission still need separate validation.

## Caller Classification

The known data slot retains the caller-configured class. Live demonstrations
accept only `synthetic-public`; text must contain no customer/private data.

## Body Bytes

The single quantity uses the manifest's byte URI, exact decimal string UTF-8
length, unit `byte`, scale `0`. It counts bytes, not JavaScript UTF-16 units.

## Body SHA256

The manifest's extension URI is required in `critical_extensions`. `extensions`
contains only that key, with lowercase 64-hex SHA-256 of the exact UTF-8 body.
It supplements, not replaces, the native-invocation binding.

## Authority and Unknowns

The experiment authorizer consumes the checked projection and separately loaded
principal/policy state. Grants couple repository, issue and class. Revocation,
principal mismatch, absent coupled grant or byte-limit violation denies.
Otherwise partial scope requires explicit `allow_partial_direct: true`; without
it, review is required. This policy accepts unknown provider descendants only
for a dedicated synthetic public test. No API response proves their absence.
Malformed policy or evaluator failure is an operational failure and withholds
dispatch, not a correct semantic denial. Policy checks and SaaS mutation are
not atomic across organizations; that time-of-check/use boundary remains.

# Bounded Runtime Pilot

This directory implements the GitHub Issue Comment Profile 1 from the pinned
companion Spec. It is an executable research/adoption example, not the OSuite
application, a general sandbox, or an independently certified standard.

## Two Complete Paths

```text
SDK or MCP request + configured context
  protocol:   JS description -> Python binding/tuple check
  structured: Python native-to-structured projection
        -> same current OPA policy -> same occurrence ledger
        -> one GitHub POST -> fresh readback
        -> confirmed, unknown, withheld, or duplicate-suppressed
```

Both paths use the same finite native-input restrictions, policy and controlled
dispatch behavior. The protocol adds a transferable description and a second
implementation's binding checks; it is not assumed faster or more accurate
than a correct direct adapter. SDK/MCP envelopes differ, so compare semantic
projections rather than treating their full wire hashes as identical.

Install and execute using [the quickstart](../docs/adoption/quickstart.md).
Results and exact retained reports are indexed [here](../reports/runtime-pilot-summary.md).

## Inputs and Outcomes

- `mapping.mjs` produces a direct **partial** effect declaration; the Python
  consumer checks it against the actual native capture and configured context.
- `authorization.mjs` invokes the pinned real OPA binary and validates its
  output. An engine/configuration failure is not counted as a policy denial.
- `gate.mjs` snapshots the native input and configured provider methods,
  validates provider identity, and reloads current policy after preparation
  and read-only preflight. Descriptor acceptance alone never permits a write.
- `ledger.mjs` reserves an occurrence with exclusive creation and durable
  state transitions. It is a same-host ledger, not a distributed transaction.
- `provider.mjs` uses Octokit with fixed GitHub API endpoints and no automatic
  POST retry. Credentials remain in memory and outside public evidence.
- `mcp-server.mjs` and `mcp-client.mjs` use the official SDK's real stdio
  initialize/list/call exchange. Unknown keys are rejected, not stripped.
- `replay.mjs` verifies retained byte identities and reruns local mapping/OPA.
  `--github` performs unauthenticated, read-only current-content checks.

The raw processing states (`accepted_partial`, `invalid_input`,
`unsupported_profile`, `untrusted_evidence`, `evaluation_failure`) are separate
from `allow`/`deny`/`review` and separate again from the observed provider result.
The external-evaluation CLI likewise seals inputs and labels separately before
running/scoring; see [its contract](../docs/adoption/external-evaluation-cli.md).

## Trust and Non-Claims

Local code, profile installation, policy files, configured principal/class,
ledger storage and host filesystem are trusted. The implementation identity is
a **declaration**, not an attested binary or proof of GitHub's internal code.
The native capture must come from the path that actually dispatches the request;
a hash cannot make a dishonest capture truthful.

GitHub explicitly documents notification behavior for comment creation. We
represent only the direct comment and retain unknown downstream recipients,
delivery, webhooks and internal descendants. Partial scope is admitted only
with the experiment's explicit policy choice on synthetic public resources.
No notification or transitive-closure completeness is claimed.

Current local authorization and the remote POST are not atomic. A revocation
after the final local check may race with dispatch. A local occurrence ledger
does not provide global exactly-once delivery, automatic crash-lock recovery,
multi-tenant isolation, distributed quota handling, or a provider idempotency key.
If delivery might have occurred, the reservation stays consumed and recovery
only queries. Missing or ambiguous observations remain unknown.

Readback must match the POST response ID when that ID is known. With a lost
acknowledgment, recovery excludes every comment ID recorded before dispatch
and requires one new exact content/actor match. Preexisting matching content
is withheld before dispatch. This test uses a dedicated issue, unique body
markers and one controlled writer. A new matching comment establishes current
content after preflight, not causal proof that this specific POST created it:
a concurrent same-account writer or provider-side mutation is outside that
attribution guarantee. This distinction is recorded in `recovery_evidence`.

The live runner records each scheduled/result step in a fsynced attempt journal,
stops new writes after an unexpected result, and refuses to reuse an issue
already containing a pilot marker. It does not silently create a new occurrence
to retry an uncertain write. Keep partial journals and the private local ledger
if interrupted; use read-only reconciliation instead of rerunning the live CLI.

## Evaluation Boundaries

The 55-case/22-intent development corpus is same-project, AI-assisted and public.
It was hidden from candidate implementers until its pre-result freeze, not
withheld from implementation development forever. The original incorrect freeze
ordering statement and its corrections are retained in the custody history.
The real live subset is eight scripted scenarios across two lanes and two
strategies, not 32 independent incidents or autonomous model decisions.

The upstream GitHub OpenAPI excerpt is genuine third-party interface material
with a pinned commit and retained MIT notice. It is not independently authored
governance labels. No outside team has yet run the external-custody protocol.
Costs include cold subprocesses and communication where measured; there is no
warm-path throughput claim, tail SLA, or broad customer-deployment qualification.
The `America/Toronto` report timezone is an editorial preference, not a
geolocation or Canadian work-location attestation.

# Action-Effect Runtime Pilot Quickstart

Editorial revision: 19 October 2026, America/Toronto (EDT, UTC-04:00);
first drafted 18 October. The bounded offline and live runs and both replays
are complete. See the [measured results](../../reports/runtime-pilot-summary.md)
and [working paper](../../paper/manuscript.md). No external evaluation occurred.

This bounded, interface-only pilot compares SDK and MCP issue-comment inputs
through effect-wire and complete structured OPA adapters. No OSuite account,
code, or purchase is required. Start offline; live execution is a separate
authorization, not the default installation check.

## 1. Install Without Provider Writes

Use Git, Node.js >=22 with npm, and Python >=3.9. The OPA installer supports
macOS and Linux on arm64/x64. Setup downloads source, packages, and an OPA
binary; it does not post GitHub comments.

The published Spec prerelease [v0.2.0-draft.1](https://github.com/OndCo/Action-Effect-Spec/releases/tag/v0.2.0-draft.1)
is at `a9b86f4b529a5e330c2a9bf1b8c4c259a7b36e40`, the current Bench
[spec-lock.json](../../spec-lock.json) pin. For a fresh checkout, create two
lowercase sibling clones and use that lock:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/OndCo/Action-Effect-Spec.git action-effect-spec
git clone https://github.com/OndCo/Action-Effect-Bench.git action-effect-bench
cd action-effect-bench
git -C ../action-effect-spec checkout --detach "$(node -p "require('./spec-lock.json').commit")"
```

Run every remaining command from the Bench root:

```sh
npm ci --prefix runtime-pilot --ignore-scripts --no-fund --no-audit
node runtime-pilot/install-tools.mjs
```

The dependency lock pins `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.32.1 and `@octokit/rest`
22.0.1. The installer verifies OPA 1.21.2 against the platform-specific SHA-256
in `runtime-pilot/tools.json`. Do not substitute a policy-engine stub.
If downloading fails, do not bypass verification; an existing binary is usable
only when its hash matches that manifest.

## 2. Test Offline and Replay

These tests and the offline evaluation need no GitHub credential and perform
no provider writes:

```sh
node --test runtime-pilot/tests/*.test.mjs
python3 -B -W error -m unittest discover -s runtime-pilot/tests -p 'test_*.py'
node runtime-pilot/offline-run.mjs
```

The runner prints a new report path under `reports/`. Keep its JSON and adjacent
`.sha256`, including failures. To check the published measured offline report:

```sh
node runtime-pilot/replay.mjs reports/runtime-pilot-offline-2026-10-19T04-23-54.715Z-6bb423.json
```

Replay checks report integrity, recorded inputs, source identity, mapping, and
OPA decisions; it does not repeat provider writes or reproduce original timing.
It refuses source or checksum mismatches. Use the recorded source revision,
retain nonzero exits, and never replace a failed report with a successful rerun.

## 3. Explicitly Authorized Live Run

**This command posts public comments. Do not run it without repository-owner
authorization.** It is fixed to `OndCo/Action-Effect-Bench`, not arbitrary
customer repositories.

The completed study used [issue #1](https://github.com/OndCo/Action-Effect-Bench/issues/1)
and created 12 comments. **Do not rerun that issue.** It is an evidence resource,
not a reusable public test target or permission for readers to post.

- Use a fresh, open dedicated issue, not a pull request, with the exact title
  `Action-Effect controlled runtime pilot`. Obtain its numeric issue number
  from the authorized owner; do not reuse an ordinary project issue.
- Authenticate GitHub CLI (`gh`) as the authorized account with appropriately
  narrow permissions. The runner obtains its credential from `gh`; never put
  tokens in commands, public bodies, or reports.
- Agree on synthetic public content, notification exposure, rate/cost limits,
  and cleanup. The live plan permits at most **12 new comment posts**. The
  runner refuses an issue containing an `action-effect-run:` marker.

Replace `NUMBER` with that approved issue number:

```sh
node runtime-pilot/live-run.mjs --issue NUMBER --confirm-owned-repo OndCo/Action-Effect-Bench
```

Lost-ACK recovery is automatically **read-only** in the runner. There is no
separate reconciliation CLI; exported `reconcileAction` operates on the original
ledger/occurrence. Preserve `runtime-pilot/.runtime-private/` privately and retain
the attempt journal and reports. Never retry an uncertain POST, delete markers
to bypass the guard, or rerun a used issue for recovery.

For a retained live report, optionally check current public GitHub content:

```sh
node runtime-pilot/replay.mjs reports/runtime-pilot-live-2026-10-19T04-26-11.245Z-731e54.json --github
```

`--github` adds read-only GETs, not new comments. It checks current content, not
historical wall-clock execution or complete provider provenance.
ID-less recovery requires complete preflight and unique new exact body/actor
matching on a dedicated single-writer issue. It is not execution attribution.

## 4. Interpret the Boundary

The pinned Spec's `profiles/github-issue-comment/README.md` binds the exact
resource, destination, body digest, and UTF-8 byte count.
`accepted_partial/declared_partial` is evidence processing, **not permission**;
authority remains separately evaluated. Applicable denials take precedence;
otherwise the owned-test policy needs explicit `allow_partial_direct: true`
to admit the partial direct scope. Notifications/webhooks remain unknown even
after comment readback.

Adopt in stages: interface review, offline adapter, non-dispatching comparison,
then a separately authorized owned-resource test. This is not customer deployment
readiness. Use the [protocol](../../PROTOCOL.md),
[measurement record](../../paper/measurement-contract.md), and
[external custody procedure](external-evaluation.md); propose concrete tests
through [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../CONTRIBUTING.md), not protected inputs in public.
Both repositories retain MIT for selected original work, with upstream notices;
this makes no standards-body, patent, or legal-clearance claim.
